### 1. Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets
* **Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (enacted via 2024 Special Session Senate Bill 1, amending K.S.A. § 79-32,110(a); unchanged between 2025 and 2026).
* **Rates & Brackets:**
  * **Married Filing Jointly:**
    * **5.2%** on Kansas taxable income not over $46,000.
    * **$2,392 plus 5.58%** on Kansas taxable income over $46,000.
  * **Single, Head of Household, or Married Filing Separately:**
    * **5.2%** on Kansas taxable income not over $23,000.
    * **$1,196 plus 5.58%** on Kansas taxable income over $23,000.
* **Official Sources:** 
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *2025 Form K-40ES Instructions*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-40es25.pdf
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *2026 Form K-40ES Instructions*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-40es26.pdf
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/booklet-25.pdf

---

### 2. Corporate Income Tax and Minimum Tax
* **Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Rates (Form K-120):**
  * **Normal Tax:** **3.5%** of Kansas taxable income.
  * **Surtax:** **3.0%** of Kansas taxable income in excess of $50,000.
  * **Combined Top Rate:** **6.5%** on Kansas taxable income over $50,000.
* **Minimum Tax:** **$0 / None** (Kansas law imposes no minimum corporate income tax; returns are filed whether or not tax is due, and tax is computed solely as a percentage of taxable income).
* **Corporate Franchise Tax:** **None** (repealed/expired for tax year 2011 and later under K.S.A. § 79-5401).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *2025 Corporate Income Tax Instructions*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-120instructions25.pdf
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *Franchise Tax*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/bataxfranchise.html

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax Rate & Local Rates
* **Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **State Rate:**
  * **6.5%** general state retailers' sales and compensating use tax rate.
  * *(Note: The state sales tax rate on qualifying food and food ingredients was phased down to 0% effective January 1, 2025, but prepared food and general sales remain at 6.5%)*.
* **Local Additions:** **Yes.** Kansas counties, incorporated cities, and special taxing districts may levy local sales taxes (ranging from 0.10% to 3.0%), which are added to the 6.5% state rate to calculate total collected tax.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *Pub. KS-1510 Sales Tax and Compensating Use Tax*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/pub1510.pdf
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *Pub. KS-1525 Business Taxes for Contractors, Subcontractors and Repairmen*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/pub1525.pdf
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *Sales (Retailers)*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/prsalesrate.html

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes
* **Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Gross Receipts / Margin Tax:** **Not found** (Kansas does not levy a general gross receipts or margin tax).
* **Corporate Franchise Tax:** **None** (eliminated for tax year 2011 and later; no capital stock or net worth franchise tax exists).
* **Financial Institutions Privilege Tax (Form K-130):** Assessed on net earnings of financial institutions in lieu of corporate income tax:
  * **Banks:** Normal tax of **1.94%** of net income, plus a surtax of **2.125%** of net income in excess of $25,000.
  * **Trust Companies and Savings & Loan Associations:** Normal tax of **1.93%** of net income, plus a surtax of **2.125%** of net income in excess of $25,000.
* **Pass-Through Entity Tax (SALT Parity Act, Form K-120S):** Electing pass-through entities are taxed at the highest individual rate under K.S.A. § 79-32,110(a), which is **5.58%**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *Privilege Tax Overview & Instructions*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/bataxprivilege.html
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *2025 Privilege Tax Instructions*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-130instructions25.pdf
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *SALT Parity Act FAQs*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/taxsaltparityfaq.html
  * Kansas Department of Revenue, *Franchise Tax*: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/bataxfranchise.html

notes:
### 1. Individual Return Due Dates & Extension Rules (TY 2025 & 2026)

* **Due Date:** Calendar-year individual income tax returns are due on or before **April 15** following the close of the tax year (e.g., April 15, 2026, for tax year 2025). When April 15 falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, the return is due the next regular workday.
* **Extensions:** 
  * Kansas does not have a separate state extension request form. 
  * An extension of time to file is granted automatically if an approved federal extension (IRS Form 4868) is obtained, or an automatic extension is applied if at least **90%** of the Kansas tax liability is paid on or before the original due date.
  * An extension to file is **not** an extension of time to pay. Unpaid tax after the original due date incurs interest (0.6667% per month / 8% per annum). If 90% was paid by the original due date, no late-filing/late-payment penalty is assessed.
  * Extension payments must be remitted on or before the original April 15 deadline using **Form K-40V** (marking the "Extension" checkbox) or through the KDOR online portal.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * KDOR Tax Calendar (Pub. KS-1515): https://www.ksrevenue.gov/taxcalendar.html
  * Form K-40V Instructions: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-40v25.pdf
  * Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form K-40 Instructions): https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-40bundle25.pdf

---

### 2. Corporate & Pass-Through Return Due Dates & Extension Rules (TY 2025 & 2026)

* **Corporate Returns (C Corporations):**
  * **Due Date:** Due **one month after the federal corporate income tax return due date** (for calendar-year filers whose federal deadline is April 15, the Kansas return is due **May 15**).
  * **Extensions:** Kansas does not have a separate corporate extension request form. Filing federal Form 7004 with the IRS automatically grants a Kansas six-month extension; the Kansas extended deadline is **one month after the extended federal due date** (e.g., **November 15** for calendar-year filers). A copy of federal Form 7004 must be enclosed with Form K-120.
  * **Extension Payment:** An extension to file is not an extension to pay. At least 90% of the tax must be paid by the original due date using **Form K-120V** (Corporate Payment Voucher) checking the "Extension payment" box to avoid penalties.
* **Pass-Through Entity Returns (Partnerships & S Corporations):**
  * **Due Date:** Due no later than the **15th day of the fourth month** following the end of the tax year (April 15 for calendar-year filers), or conforms to the federal due date.
  * **Extensions:** Kansas does not have a separate state extension request form. Filing federal Form 7004 with the IRS automatically provides a **six-month extension** for Partnerships and S Corporations when a copy is attached to the return.
  * An extension of time to file Form K-120S does not extend the time for filing a partner’s or shareholder’s individual return. If tax is due at the entity level, payments are made with Form K-120V.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * KDOR Tax Calendar (Pub. KS-1515): https://www.ksrevenue.gov/taxcalendar.html
  * Corporate Income Tax Instructions: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-120booklet25.pdf
  * Partnership or S Corporation Income Tax Booklet: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-120sinstructions25.pdf

---

### 3. Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET) (TY 2025 & 2026)

* **Existence:** Yes. Enacted under the Kansas **SALT Parity Act** (K.S.A. 79-32,286 et seq.).
* **Tax Rate:** 
  * Under K.S.A. 79-32,287, the tax rate for 2024 and beyond is set to the highest individual income tax rate under K.S.A. 79-32,110(a). 
  * Following the individual rate adjustments enacted in 2024, the highest individual income tax bracket is **5.58%**.
  * The PTET rate on Form K-120S (Line 32) and Form K-9 is **5.58%** for tax year 2025 (and remains 5.58% for 2026 unless statutory revenue trigger decreases occur).
* **How and When to Elect:**
  * The election is made **annually** on the timely filed Kansas Partnership or S Corporation return (**Form K-120S**) for the tax year by checking **Box N** ("Mark this box if electing to be subject to tax at the entity level"). 
  * (Box O is marked if electing to tax 100% of the income of resident owners).
  * Eligible owners include resident and nonresident individual partners/shareholders and trusts; corporations and upper-tier partnerships are not eligible. 
  * The entity reports each owner’s share of tax paid on **Form K-9**, which the owner encloses with Form K-40 (Line 25) or Form K-41 (Line 16) to claim a credit.
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * KDOR SALT Parity FAQ: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/saltparityfaq.html
  * Form K-120S and Instructions: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-120sinstructions25.pdf
  * Form K-9: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-9_24.pdf

---

### 4. Composite or Group Nonresident Returns (TY 2025 & 2026)

* **Composite Return Rules:** 
  * A partnership or S corporation may elect to file a composite return on behalf of nonresident partners or nonresident shareholders who derive income from the entity.
  * Written prior approval from KDOR is **not** required.
  * Nonresident owners included on a composite return cannot have any Kansas-source income other than from the entity. They must use the standard deduction, are not entitled to pass-through credits or charitable contribution deductions, and are relieved from filing a separate Kansas individual return.
  * **Forms Used:** **Schedule K-40C** (Composite Income Tax Schedule) is completed and attached to a Kansas Individual Income Tax Return (**Form K-40**) filed under the **partnership's or S corporation's name and EIN**. The pass-through entity also marks **Box L** on Form K-120S.
  * **Due Date:** Schedule K-40C/Form K-40 must be filed and tax paid on or before the **15th day of the fourth month** following the close of the entity's tax year (April 15 for calendar-year filers).
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Schedule K-40C Instructions: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-40c25.pdf
  * Partnership/S Corporation Instructions: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-120sinstructions25.pdf

---

### 5. Estimated Tax Requirements & Pass-Through Nonresident Withholding

* **Individual Estimated Tax:**
  * Required if the Kansas income tax balance due after withholding and credits is **$500 or more**, and withholding/prepaid credits are less than **90%** of the current year’s tax liability or **100%** of the prior year’s tax liability.
  * Due dates for calendar-year filers: **April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15** of the following tax year. Form **K-40ES**.
* **Corporate Estimated Tax:**
  * Required if corporate income tax liability can reasonably be expected to exceed **$500** (not required in the corporation's first year of existence in Kansas).
  * Due dates: 15th day of the **4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months** of the corporate tax year (April 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15 for calendar-year filers). Form **K-120ES**.
* **Pass-Through Entity Estimated Tax (Elective PTET):**
  * Under the SALT Parity Act, an electing pass-through entity is treated as a C corporation for estimated tax purposes and must make estimated payments if tax liability exceeds **$500**.
  * Due dates are the same as corporate estimated taxes (15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th, and 12th months) remitted via Form **K-120ES** or online. Underpayment penalty is calculated on **Schedule K-220S**.
* **Pass-Through Nonresident Withholding:**
  * **Repealed:** Mandatory nonresident withholding on pass-through entity owners (formerly under K.S.A. 79-32,100e and Forms KW-7 / KW-7S) was repealed by the Kansas Legislature effective July 1, 2014 (Notice 14-09).
  * For tax years 2025 and 2026, Kansas has **no mandatory pass-through nonresident withholding requirement**. Nonresident owners satisfy tax liabilities either by filing Form K-40, participating in a composite return (K-40/K-40C), or having tax paid on their behalf via the elective PTET (Form K-120S).
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Form K-40ES Instructions: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-40es25.pdf
  * Form K-120ES Instructions: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/k-120es25.pdf
  * KDOR Notice 14-09 (Withholding Repealed For Nonresident PTE Owners): https://www.ksrevenue.gov/taxpolicy.html

---

### 6. Main Return Forms (TY 2025 & 2026)

* **Individual Income Tax:** **Form K-40** (*Kansas Individual Income Tax Return*)
* **Corporate Income Tax:** **Form K-120** (*Kansas Corporation Income Tax Return*)
* **Pass-Through Entities (Partnership / S Corporation):** **Form K-120S** (*Kansas Partnership or S Corporation Income Tax Return*)
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * KDOR Individual Income Tax Forms: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/iitaxforms.html
  * KDOR Corporate Tax Forms: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/corptaxforms.html
